Navigation · Cranial & Spine Field Guide

Register. Calibrate. Navigate.

Real-time image-guided navigation on the Curve platform — from AIRO intraoperative CT spine workflows to VarioGuide cranial biopsy trajectories.

CURVE NAVIGATION AIRO CT VARIOGUIDE

Curve Navigation Cart

Optical & EM tracking
Monitor Cart + Camera Cart. Infrared camera measures reflective marker arrays on instruments & patient for real-time optical tracking.
  1. Remove protection covers from the Monitor Cart and Camera Cart; move both to position and lock all brakes.
  2. Connect the Camera Cart to the Monitor Cart via direct ethernet at the Connection Panel.
  3. Plug both carts into wall power, then press the power button on the back of the monitor to start.
  4. Press the laser button on the camera handle and use the beam to center the operating field in the camera’s view.
Best position: Camera Cart at the foot of the bed, Monitor Cart within the surgeon’s line of sight.

iTouchscreen Adjustment

  • Height — 1.2–1.5 m. Hold the sides of the monitor and lift/push to adjust.
  • Tilt — 5° to 22.5°. Hold the sides and tilt to suit the procedure.

iLoading Patient Data (Curve)

  1. Insert media (USB into the connection panel, or CD into the drive).
  2. Select the desired patient — check the filter on the left is correct — then Ok.
  3. Select the dataset from the timeline and Ok to open the home screen.

Merge Duplicate Patients

Preoperatively & intraoperatively · Patient Selection

1Preoperatively

  1. Open Patient Selection > the Manage drop-down > select Merge.
  2. With Merge activated, select the two duplicate patients — they highlight orange — then select Merge at the top left.
  1. Select the target patient in the dialog (a previously-selected patient is auto-selected as the target) and confirm with Ok. All images become available under the merged patient.
Merged the wrong two patients? Go to Patient Selection and select Restore at any time to undo.

2Intraoperatively

If new patient images are imported intraoperatively and a conflicting-patient-data dialog appears:

  • Merge received images with current patient (Ok) if they’re the same person, to combine the duplicates.
  • Switch to patient of received images if the patients are different and you want to restart the workflow on the new images — instrument calibration and/or validation must be repeated.
  • Cancel to ignore the received images — this makes the intraoperative device data unusable in the navigation app.
Pro tip: use patient names/IDs from a worklist or the hospital PACS rather than manual entry, to avoid duplicate patient records in the first place.

Move, Park & Store Airo

Hardware: Airo
  1. Ensure the table top is removed, then insert the key and rotate to On; press Start.
  2. Select Transport from the Choose Mode screen (or Menu > Transport on the pendant).
  3. Latch: with the gantry at the end of the rail, rotate and align it with the base until it latches.
  4. Disconnect all power/network cables, then press Up on the pendant to raise Airo onto its wheels.
  5. Move using the forward/reverse buttons and side-handles — Airo weighs 975 kg (2150 lb).
  6. Park in OR: select Scan, press Down to lower the base, then plug in power/network.
!

Collision risk. Inclines must not exceed 5° and thresholds must not exceed 9.5 mm (3/8″). Confirm nothing is underneath Airo before lowering.

iTransfer Table Top to Column

  1. Set the shuttle to zero position, 5th wheel pedal to freewheel, brake pedal unbraked.
  2. Place the shuttle against the column and hold Transfer (shuttle) or Zero Position (remote) until the column reaches upper lift.
  3. Transfer the table top onto the column, avoiding collision with the gantry. A two-tone signal confirms Table top (type) recognized.
  4. Move the shuttle away once the signal sounds.

OR Setup & Scanning Position

Ensure the area is safe for X-ray exposure
!

Before scanning: markers on Airo visible to the camera, patient ≥5 cm from the bore, staff shielded or clear of the room.

Lumbar–Thoracic

Feet-first, camera positioned opposite the gantry. Gantry moves to the end of the rail for operating access — use a 4-marker array for any 90° table rotation.

Cervical Spine

Head facing away from the camera at the table base. Four operating positions are supported (0°/90°/180° rotation and close-proximity) — the surgeon must stand clear of the unsterile gantry.

Cranial

Radiolucent reference array, head clamp and pins required. Camera and reference array position must stay fixed between scan and surgery.

What You Need

Instrument setup & calibration
ICM4 Calibration Block. Confirm every reflective marker sphere is screwed on firmly before commencing calibration.
Brainlab MIS Spine TrayMinimum requirement
Spinal OpenAwls & probes
Brainlab Drill GuideI & II systems
ICM4 BlockCalibration reference
On Curve, select Instrument Setup from the Navigation section to begin.

Drill Guide I Assembly

2.4 mm cervical · 3.2 mm thoracolumbar
  1. Insert the drill guide tube into the array — reverse thread. Match the size on the neck to the drill bit.
  2. Assemble the black handle, array and depth-control ruler — ensure the handle teeth seat in the array grooves.
  3. Fit the small nut onto the bolt (roughly halfway), insert, and set the desired depth with the ruler.

iCalibrating Drill Guide I

  1. Open Sets from the menu, then select Brainlab – Drilling.
  2. Find the Drill Guide matching your array (3-Ball or 4-Ball) and pick the diameter (2.4 / 2.6 / 3.2 mm).
  3. Tap the instrument image to open calibration, then Calibrate.
  4. Nurse inserts the drill guide into the 5 mm hole on the ICM4 block and rotates to complete.

Drill Guide II Assembly

Quick-release, dual depth-stop
  1. Insert the drill guide tube into the array base — hold the blue button down to insert and release to secure.
  2. Slide the black handle onto the array base.
  3. Attach the spring, align the two grey dots, push in and twist to secure. Rotate the blue nut to the desired depth — push firmly until it clicks.
  4. Attach the array to the drill guide. Test by passing the drill bit down the guide; the handle can be repositioned after calibration.

iCalibrating Drill Guide II

Same workflow as Drill Guide I — Sets > Brainlab – Drilling, match array & diameter, tap to calibrate, then rotate in the ICM4 hole to confirm.

Single Instruments

Awl · Probe · Tap · Screwdriver · Pedicle Access Needle

1Pedicle Access Needle (Jamshidi)

  1. Single Instruments > Other > Brainlab Pedicle Access Needle > Calibrate.
  2. Ensure the disposable trocar is opened and inserted, then Calibrate.
  3. Nurse rotates in the pivot point (ICM4) to complete.
Array geometry is the same as the Medium StarLink Array.

2Awl

  1. Set up with the 4-ball array and straight handle.
  2. Single Instruments > Awl > select 3.0 or 4.0 mm > Calibrate.
  3. Nurse rotates in the pivot point to complete.

3Probe

  1. Set up with the 3-ball array and gear-shift handle — notch faces the array’s ‘1’ position.
  2. Single Instruments > Probe > select 3.5 or 4.5 mm > Calibrate.

4Tap

  1. Attach the Small StarLink Array and tighten with the silver T-handle.
  2. Single Instruments > Other > Screwdriver/Tap > Calibrate.
  3. Select the receptacle diameter matching your tap; nurse holds and rotates in the pivot point.
  4. Adjust to the correct diameter and accept on the blue verification area.

5Screwdriver

  1. Attach the Large StarLink Array and tighten with the silver T-handle.
  2. Select the receptacle diameter matching your loaded screw; rotate in the pivot point.
  3. Use the sliders to set the correct screw diameter and length, then Accept.
Use the Small Array on a second screwdriver to have two calibrated at once.

Airo Daily QA

Pre-surgery maintenance · hardware: Airo
  1. Warm Up Scan — Menu > Warm Up, clear the area, select & hold Scan, then Next if successful.
  2. E-Stop Test — Hospital Service > E-Stop Test. Hold Scan until the gantry moves and beeps, then press E-Stop — the beep must stop within 0.5 s.
  3. Gain Calibration — allow 30 min warm-up, Hospital Service > Gain Calibration, clear the field of view, hold Scan.
  4. Quality Check Scan — Hospital Service > Quality Check Scans > Daily Helical/Axial QC, align the phantom & lasers, hold Scan until the pendant light goes out.
!

Contact Brainlab if the Emergency Stop Test fails.

Patient & Workflow Selection

Curve
  1. Patient Selection loads automatically — no details needed, select OK bottom-right.
  2. From Workflow selection under Spine & Trauma, select 3D Navigation.

Connect Curve ↔ Airo

  • Connect the Curve Monitor Cart and Airo with an ethernet cable.
  • Curve: labelled ‘Airo’ port on the back of the system.
  • Airo: labelled ‘Curve’ port on the left of the base.
On Curve, select Airo Auto-Registration under the Registration heading — within Cranial Navigation use Register > Automatic Registration Airo; within Spine & Trauma use Register > New Scan > Airo Scanner.
No user interaction on Curve is required during the registration workflow once connected.

iCamera Indicators

  • Both Patient Reference and Scanner indicators must show green before scanning — reposition the camera if needed.
  • The radiographer must select With Navigation on Airo before this turns green — only possible before the scout scan.

Scan Patient

Hardware: Airo & Curve pendant
  1. New Scan > New Patient (or load existing) > enter details > Next.
  2. Enter patient weight — Airo auto-calculates dose (110 lb/50 kg minimum dose; 400 lb/180 kg table limit).
  3. Confirm the ring rotation for imaging and that markers are visible to the camera > Next.
  4. Select region & scan mode, e.g. Spine > Lumbar > Helical > Next.
  5. Set Kernel, Field of View and Navigation (must be checked for auto-registration) > Next.
  6. Select the patient’s orientation and position > Next.
  7. Choose A-P, Lateral, or Skip Scout Scan > Next.

Finalize Scan

  1. Collision-check the drape and patient’s arms; set the 2D scout scan start/end points > Next.
  2. Review parameters, clear the room, then press & hold Scan for the scout duration.
  3. Define the 3D scan area — Left Bound, Right Bound, Field of View (min/max length 79–300 mm) > Next.
  4. Hold Move to send the gantry to the start position — the 3D scan prepares automatically.
  5. If helical + A-P scout: choose Constant or Modulated Tube Current.
  6. Wait for both marker arrays to show a check mark, clear the room, and hold Scan (≈15 s) until Performing 3D Scan completes.

Verify Registration Accuracy

  • Data sends automatically from Airo to Curve once the scan completes.
  • Hold the pointer tip to at least three known anatomical landmarks and confirm on-screen positions.
  • Bring the Brainlab Pointer into camera view to enable the Yes button.
  • Check accuracy in every direction — cranial/caudal, medial/lateral, anterior/posterior.

Screw Planning

Curve · Spine & Trauma 3D Navigation
  1. Select Screw Planning from the menu.
  2. Adjust Diameter and Length to match the screw loaded on the calibrated screwdriver.
  3. Set Offset to match the length used when the screwdriver was calibrated.
  4. Select Store — the planned screw turns blue once saved.

iFine Tuning

Open Fine Tuning to toggle between stored screws and adjust trajectory, diameter, length or offset for any plan without re-drawing it from scratch.

!

Diameter & length must match the loaded implant — a mismatch between the planned screw and the calibrated instrument will misrepresent trajectory accuracy on screen.

Navigation – Windowing

To see bone more clearly, open the View dropdown > Windowing (always required for Ziehm scans).

  • Right → Left drag — contrast adjustment
  • Up → Down drag — brightness adjustment

Live Trajectory Guidance

Drill Guide · Awl · Tap · Screwdriver

Once an instrument is calibrated and the patient is registered, its split-screen view tracks the planned trajectory in real time:

  • Left/axial and right/sagittal (or in-line) panes show the instrument overlaid on the planned screw path.
  • A live Tip Distance readout reports offset from the planned trajectory in millimetres.
  • Diameter and length sliders on the right update the projected implant outline as you adjust them.
  • Confirm alignment on the highlighted blue verification area before proceeding, and accept when prompted “Do you accept the calibration accuracy?”

iDrilling the Pilot Hole

With Drill Guide I or II navigated along the planned trajectory, advance to the depth set on the drill guide’s ruler/blue-nut stop (Step 3 of assembly) while keeping the guide centred in the crosshair on-screen.

iTapping & Screw Placement

Follow the same live-navigation view with the calibrated Tap, then the Screwdriver — both display the loaded implant’s diameter/length directly over the planned trajectory so final position can be confirmed before the screw is seated.

!

Reduce respiration and avoid moving the patient, table, or camera once trajectory guidance is active — any array or camera movement invalidates the live accuracy readout.

Setup for Cranial Navigation

Curve · rigid fixation is everything
  • Ensure rigid fixation of the patient in the head holder — the system cannot compensate for head movement.
  • Fix the reference array close to the region of interest (ROI). A warning is shown if it is placed too far away.
  • Be careful during draping that the array and holder do not shift.
  • Choose a camera position that will work for the whole procedure — ideally on the same side as the reference array.
  • Minimise camera movement after registration; re-verify accuracy any time it must be moved.

iPointer Accuracy Check

Before placing marker spheres on the Pointer, check that the tip aligns with the counter pin of the Pointer Gauge. Once sterile, you can optionally place the tip in the divot at the centre of the Patient Reference Array from Instrument Options to display a live accuracy value in mm.

Registration Instruments

Unsterile & sterile pointers
Z-touch. Emits an infrared laser beam detected by the camera. Press the yellow button to activate; ensure both the LED and the laser point are visible to the camera.
Softouch. Electronic pointer with a skin-detection sensor. Press the power button to initiate; ensure the reflective spheres and LED are visible to the camera.
An unsterile patient reference array is also required for registration — it is removed once the patient is draped and replaced with a sterile array.

Marker Sphere Care

  • Use new marker spheres for every unsterile and sterile instrument and array.
  • Ensure all spheres are mounted correctly before use.
  • Never navigate with dirty, damaged, wet or covered spheres — check condition throughout the case.
  • Clean visibly dirty or wet spheres with a wet wipe, then a dry wipe.
  • Discard all marker spheres at the end of each case.

Attach the Tracking Array

StarLink · EM Instrument Tracker
  • Attach the largest StarLink array possible to the instrument adapter.
  • If using an adapter clamp, confirm it is secure and won’t move in use.
  • Where possible, run the long arm of the array parallel to the instrument’s long axis.
  • Fix the array tightly to the instrument with the screwdriver.

Open Instrument Calibration

Show the instrument and the Instrument Calibration Matrix (ICM4) to the camera to open the calibration dialog automatically — available from Instrument Options.

1Pivot Point Calibration

  1. Place the instrument tip in a pivot point and rotate slightly.
  2. Hold steady as the progress bar fills, then verify accuracy on screen.
Best suited to pointed-tip instruments. Curved instruments can be calibrated, but their axis remains uncalibrated.

2Holes Calibration

  1. Select Holes from the instrument calibration dialog.
  2. Place the instrument in the smallest hole it fits while touching the base of the ICM4.
  3. Tap the corresponding hole on screen and hold the instrument still until the progress bar is full.
  4. Verify the calibration by following the on-screen instructions.

3Notch Calibration

  1. Select Notch from the instrument calibration dialog.
  2. Place the tip in the pivot point and rotate slightly.
  3. Slide the instrument onto the notch and hold still until the progress bar is full.
!

Don’t calibrate conical instruments using Notch calibration.

Calibration Verification

After a successful calibration the distance to the verification point is shown. Select Yes if satisfactory to open the navigation screen, or No to recalibrate. Confirm against known anatomical landmarks before proceeding.

iIf Calibration Fails

  • Keep the instrument tip right-angled (90°) both times.
  • Place the tip gently in the divot point — without pressure.
  • Only calibrate rigid instruments.
  • Keep the instrument and pointer centred in the tracking volume.
Attaching a new instrument to the same tracker/StarLink array always requires a new calibration.

Preparing for Registration

  1. Select the patient, confirming the correct database (PACS, CD/USB, etc.).
  2. Select the Cranial Navigation workflow, then Navigation.
  3. Select the relevant data for the procedure > Next.
  4. Optionally review the data in Viewer, or pre-op plan in Smartbrush / Trajectory Planning.
  5. When ready, select Registration from the home screen.
The Registration app defaults to Surface Matching. If the patient has fiducials, switch to Landmark from the drop-down menu.

Surface Matching Registration

Uses the skin surface · Z-touch or Softouch

1Position the Camera

Choose one camera position for the entire procedure. Verify visibility of the pointer and microscope using the Camera app.

2Position the Patient Reference Array

Position the array as close to the region of interest (ROI) as possible — within 45 cm. Ensure the array and head are securely fixed in the skull clamp to maintain accuracy.

3Verify the 3D Reconstruction

Before acquiring points, compare the 3D model’s surface with the real patient in the skull clamp. If the reconstruction is unsatisfactory, adjust the threshold, switch datasets, or exclude dissimilar areas.

4Acquire Guide & Surface Points

  • Acquire three guide points sequentially, in the order shown — gently touch the patient with the Softouch tip.
  • If a point is unavailable, select Skip Point; use Edit Point to reposition manually.
  • Slowly acquire points over the green area with Softouch and/or Z-touch, including both sides of the nose bridge (excluding the tip).
  • Acquire points on both sides of the face, near the ROI, and at the top of the head.
  • Avoid loose skin, deformed areas, and any regions that may have shifted (taped/swollen skin, non-rigid areas).
  • Hold Z-touch perpendicular to the skin with the laser point and diode visible to the camera; move Softouch slow and steady — do not trace or press.
Calculate activates once the progress bar reaches 50% — start it manually, or keep acquiring and let the software proceed automatically.
!

Prone position: tilt the table and reference array toward the camera side, start acquisition promptly before facial swelling, and settle the camera in its final position early — registration and navigation views differ, so it typically can’t be moved again.

Landmark (Fiducial) Registration

Paired-point matching · Softouch or Pointer
  • A minimum of 4 fiducials is required — we recommend placing 8–12. Circle each with a marking pen in case it falls off.
  • Position fiducials randomly around the head, far apart (avoid symmetry or a straight line), surrounding the ROI.
  • Avoid loose skin, including areas near the head-clamp pins.
  • Recommended sites: right & left mastoid process, forehead midline, forehead hairline (L/R), behind each ear, occipital midline, and around the ROI.
  1. Switch the registration method from Surface Match to Landmark.
  2. Tap each fiducial on the 3D view — semi-automatic detection activates near the marker centre.
  3. Fine-adjust by dragging the circled crosshair in the axial, coronal and sagittal views; plan points slightly deep to the skin to allow for skin shift.
  4. Register activates once enough points are planned (at least 4). Acquire each in the listed order — a green tick confirms acquisition.
  5. Select Calculate to proceed, or let it happen automatically once all points are acquired.
!

Use 6–7+ markers where possible. Skip any fiducial that looks deformed or has shifted — most often behind the ear or at the back of the head. Hold the pointer perpendicular to the landmark.

iVerify Registration Accuracy

Hold the pointer to widely distributed landmarks — both sides of the face, tip of the nose, inner ear — and select Yes if satisfactory. If not, select No for More Points, Start Over, or to switch registration method.

Rescue Registration

Optional safeguard · does not improve accuracy
!

Rescue registration does not improve accuracy — an accurate initial registration is essential. Set it up before any incident, like fastening a seatbelt. Use it if registration is lost to accidental reference movement or a head shift in the clamp.

Start after the craniotomy screen by selecting Yes in the rescue registration dialog, or open Rescue Planning in Content Manager at any time.

iAcquire & Manage Rescue Points

  • Use ≥5 identifiable landmarks (bone screws, small drill divots) at least 1 cm apart, accessible throughout surgery.
  • Hold the pointer tip perpendicular to the landmark and slowly pivot; select Accept once acquired.

Select a rescue point’s name to activate it (turns orange) before re-acquiring, or use the trash icon to remove it. Calculate becomes active once 5 points are acquired.

If registration is lost intra-operatively, open Rescue Registration, re-register from the saved points, then verify accuracy using different landmarks from the rescue points.

VarioGuide 1.0 Assembly (RHH)

Legacy gold & black arm · Royal Hobart Hospital

The original VarioGuide arm assembles as a mirror image for left- vs. right-sided biopsies — the array holder and Joint 2 bolt move to the opposite side of Joint 1 depending on approach.

Left-sided biopsy: array holder opposite Joint 1, Joint 2 bolt on the same side as Joint 1. Right-sided biopsy: array holder on the same side as Joint 1, Joint 2 bolt opposite Joint 1.

1Build the Arm & Array Holder

  1. Place the disc joint into the VarioGuide arm, then rotate it 180° until the two lines align.
  2. Tighten Joint 1 and check it sits flush with the disc joint.
  3. Line up the two lines on the outside of the disc.
  4. Push the array holder (the “lollipop”) into the Joint 2 opening — push in, rotate clockwise, then push in again.
  5. Push the holder in until it sits between the + and − marks and the horizontal line matches the line on the disc joint, then tighten Joint 2.
  6. Fit the reference array (3 balls) onto Joint 3.

2Fit & Secure the Reference Array

  1. Rotate the array so its arms face away from the VarioGuide holder, then push it into the holder — it only fits one way — and rotate it 90°.
  2. Tighten Joint 3 and ensure it sits flush with the array holder.
  3. Check the two lines on the joint line up (highlighted in green on the Wizard).
  4. Place the black disc (1.8–2.0 mm) onto the array, ensuring the other half is connected to the black tightening disc — the two halves simply click together.
  5. Line up the two lines on the disc so the 1.8–2.0 mm position matches, then rotate the outer disc to tighten.
Once assembled, the VarioGuide 1.0 attaches to the headholder or V-Adapter in either the left- or right-arm position.

VarioGuide 2.0 Assembly (CLV)

Current arm with A–B–C markings · Calvary Hospital
  1. Place the disc joint onto the ring of the VarioGuide arm — teeth match the indentations, one orientation only.
  2. Rotate the disc joint 180° until the two lines align, insert the Joint 1 lock and tighten.
  3. Screw the tracking-array holder in until it slides freely, then tighten Joint 2 to secure it.
  4. Fit the VarioGuide array (one orientation only), turn it 90°, insert the Joint 3 lock and tighten.

iFit the Guide Disc

  1. Select the disc set containing the diameter required for your instrument.
  2. Press the inner disc onto the array until it clicks, aligned to the arrow.
  3. Assemble and screw the lock ring into place.
Assembly differs slightly for left vs. right T-Adapter placement — match Joints 2 & 3 to the A–A or B–B markings shown in the Wizard.

iOpen the VarioGuide Wizard

After registering the patient, open Instrument Options > Tools > VarioGuide. Select Assembly for a step-by-step walkthrough video (toggle left/right setup), or Verification to check accuracy.

!

Attach the VarioGuide on the same side as the lesion (supine or prone) with the Patient Reference on the opposite side. Keep the VarioGuide visible to the camera throughout — a prone position may suit deep lesions better.

Align & Perform Biopsy

Once the VarioGuide is connected, check the marker spheres are facing the camera — if not, perform a 180° turn of Joints 2 & 3.

  1. Drape the patient, then puncture the drape and screw the VarioGuide onto the T-Adapter — ensure marker spheres face the camera (180° turn of Joints 2 & 3 if not).
  2. Activate the Wizard, roughly position the arm over the planned entry point, and tighten once prompted to Lock Joint.
  3. Follow the Wizard’s coarse and fine adjustment steps, aligning each joint as close to 0° as possible before selecting Proceed.
Tip: if the adjustment value isn’t showing, loosen the joint and make a bigger movement so the camera detects it. At the final step the Wizard shows the maximum and mean target deviation — keep adjusting until you’re happy with the value, then accept to save the setup.

iMark & Create the Burr Hole

  1. Once the VarioGuide is aligned, pass the Biopsy Needle through it until it touches the skin, marking the entry point.
  2. Ask the surgeon to drop the needle onto the skin and draw around the point with a sterile marker for burr hole placement.
  3. Gently loosen Joint 1 to swing the arm clear, then tighten Joint 1 again so the arm stays locked out of the way while the surgeon creates the burr hole.
  4. Once the burr hole is made, loosen Joint 1 again and bring the arm back to centre to realign — that’s the only joint that needs to move. Confirm on the verification screen that every joint shows green.

iReminders

  • Verify marker-sphere condition before use — not dirty, damaged or wet.
  • Keep joints as close to 0° as possible during setup for best alignment.
  • Once aligned, swapping guide discs can shift the VarioGuide alignment — check the fitted disc carefully.
  • Handle VarioGuide parts carefully to avoid pinched fingers or punctured gloves.

iOptional: Verify Accuracy

VarioGuide accuracy: assemble the VarioGuide, open the Tools menu, select Instruments > VarioGuide, then follow the guide and hold the pointer to the divots on the disc.

Biopsy needle accuracy: position the guide disc so the needle can be inserted vertically.

  1. Insert the Disposable Biopsy Needle Type A into the guide disc until Stop is highlighted in blue — the arrows indicate which direction to adjust the needle to reach the insertion depth.
  2. Tighten the lock ring to secure the needle in the guide disc.
  3. The software calculates and displays the needle’s trajectory deviation, based on the coordinates of the needle’s tracking array and the VarioGuide tracking array.

Plan a Trajectory

Trajectories can be created in three applications — Trajectory Planning, Instrument Options, or intra-operatively in Cranial Navigation. In every case, the entry must sit on the skull surface and the target within the lesion for correct VarioGuide alignment.

A trajectory doesn’t have to be pre-planned. You can instead drill the burr hole first, then use a pointer intra-operatively in Cranial Navigation to acquire the trajectory directly at the surgical site once the desired path is confirmed — the same Offset workflow as Step 3 below.

iEntry & Target Points

Entry (E): the point on the skull/scalp surface where the instrument enters. Target (T): the point within the lesion the instrument is aimed at. Together the two points define the trajectory line the VarioGuide will align to.

Things for the surgeon to weigh up when choosing E and T: the shortest safe path into the lesion, entering as close to perpendicular to the skull as practical, avoiding sulci, major vessels and eloquent cortex along the path, and making sure the entry point is actually reachable given the patient’s position and headholder/clamp setup.

Changing E or T: in the Trajectory Planning app, simply click and drag the E or T handle to a new position on any view. In Instrument Options, select the trajectory and use Set Entry / Set Target again to redefine either point — both update live and the software re-checks entry-on-skull / target-in-lesion validity.

Scrolling the trajectory with the surgeon: use the Review tab (Instrument Options) for a Probe’s-Eye view along the planned path, or scroll through the axial/sagittal/coronal slices in Trajectory Planning, so the surgeon can check for potential landmarks — vessels, ventricles, sulci — the whole length of the trajectory before it’s confirmed.

  1. Trajectory Planning app: select Trajectory from the Cranial Workflow > Create New > drag the E (entry) and T (target) points into position > adjust name/colour via Properties > Ok to save.
  1. Instrument Options app: Data > Trajectories > Create New > drag the crosshairs, then Set Entry / Set Target > review with the Probe’s-Eye view > Confirm.
  1. Intra-operative (Cranial Navigation): open the Offset drop-down, toggle Use Offset, adjust the virtual tip with the slider or +/− buttons, then Acquire to store it as a trajectory. This is the option to use if you’re planning with the pointer after the burr hole has already been made, rather than pre-planning on the scan.
The virtual extension shows as a red line with a crosshair tip; the actual instrument shows in green.

iPrepare & Insert the Biopsy Needle

Once alignment is confirmed, the distance-to-target is displayed. Set the needle stopper using Stopper Distance = VarioGuide-to-Target + 50 mm (disc diameter).

Cutting window: red line on the green line — the cutting window is closed. Red line on the red line — the cutting window is open. Keep the needle closed throughout insertion and align red-on-red only once at the target.
Tip: the surgeon may choose to aspirate as the needle reaches the target — gentle aspiration can help confirm the needle is within the lesion before the cutting window is opened and the sample taken.
Offer the surgeon a minimum volume extension tube — ask anaesthetics for one. Connecting it between the syringe and the needle lets the surgeon aspirate and rotate the needle clockwise without having to hold the needle itself while doing so.
!

The reflective markers on the Biopsy Needle rotate 360° — line of sight can be maintained without rotating the cutting window itself.

EM Tracking System

Hardware: Kick EM · Curve EM

The EM unit ships in a padded transport case containing the EM Base Station, EM Field Generator with positioning arm, and all cabling.

  • EM Base Station — interface box connecting the system to Curve.
  • EM Field Generator — creates the electromagnetic tracking volume.
  • EM Field Generator Positioning Arm — mounts the generator to the OR table.
  • EM Power/Data Cable — links the generator to the Base Station.

Connect & Mount the System

  1. Ensure the Monitor Cart is switched off before starting setup.
  2. Attach the EM Field Generator positioning arm to the rail of the OR table.
  3. Pull the locking lever forward and mount the EM Field Generator onto the arm, then push the lever inward to lock.
For optimum accuracy, position the Field Generator 10–35 cm from the patient’s head, out of the surgeon’s way, with the yellow stripe facing the patient’s head.
!

Connect all cables before turning the system on.

iConnect the EM Base Station

  1. Connect the power plug to the Base Station’s power port, and the data plug to the navigation system port.
  2. Connect the USB plug to the labelled USB port, and the accessory power plug to the Monitor Cart connection panel.
  3. Connect the EM Field Generator cable to the Base Station, then mount the Base Station on the OR table rail.

iTurn On & Initiate Software

  1. Connect the Monitor Cart’s mains cable to a wall outlet, then press the power button on the back to start.
  2. Select the patient > select the patient scan(s) > select EM Navigation from the Cranial workflow > Setup Navigation.
  3. Follow the setup wizard.

EM Instruments

1Unsterile

Patient Reference EM, EM Registration Pointer and Instrument Adapter EM (for Disposable Stylet) — connect to the instrument ports of the EM Base Station as required.

2Sterile

EM Pointer (20 sterilisation cycles), Instrument Adapter EM (20 sterilisation cycles) and Disposable EM Stylet.

Mount the Patient Reference

  1. Select a position where skin shift is unlikely.
  2. Prepare the skin — clean, dry and remove hair.
  3. Tape Patient Reference EM to the skin.
  4. Loop the cable and tape it to the head for strain relief.
  5. Connect the Patient Reference EM to an instrument port on the EM Base Station.

Adjust the Field Generator and patient so the reference sits within the optimal tracking volume shown in the setup wizard. Position paediatric patients at the head of the table to avoid EM interference.

!

Do not operate within 20 cm of an installed pacemaker.

Attach the EM Instrument Reference

  1. Place the EM Instrument Reference securely into the StarLink interface so the teeth line up.
  2. Tighten the fixation screw until it cannot be turned any further.
  3. Connect the EM Instrument Reference to an instrument port.
Attaching a new instrument to the same reference always requires a new calibration.

Calibrate the Instrument

  1. Bring the instrument into the tracking volume to open the calibration dialog automatically.
  2. Place the instrument tip in the EM Pointer divot point and press the button.
  3. Hold the instrument steady until the progress bar is full.

Slowly rotate the instrument ~50° until the rotation progress bar fills, then hold it steady for a few seconds as the final progress bar fills.

Select Yes if the distance to tip is satisfactory, then confirm registration accuracy on known anatomical landmarks.

iIf Calibration Fails

  • Keep the instrument tip right-angled (90°) both times.
  • Place the tip gently in the divot point — without pressure.
  • Only calibrate rigid instruments.
  • Keep the reference-to-tip distance under 20 cm, with only the instrument being calibrated, the EM Pointer and the EM Patient Reference in the tracking volume.
Attaching a new instrument to the same reference always requires a new calibration.

Troubleshooting

iSources of EM Interference

  • Devices: EM Base Station and Curve Monitor Cart should be ≥60 cm from the EM Field Generator.
  • Cabling: don’t wrap the EM Field Generator cable around itself while in use.
  • Instruments: some older StarLink clamps and endoscopes, Blakesley clamps and microdebriders.
  • Other: anaesthesia equipment, endoscope towers, instrument tables, the OR table and lamps, mobile phones, monitors, piercings or watches.

iTracking Volume Smaller Than Usual

  • Identify the bad tracking area using the EM Pointer (sterile) or EM Registration Pointer (unsterile).
  • Find a local source of interference from the list above.
  • Move equipment around to achieve maximal volume.
  • Place a foam pad between the table and patient if the OR table itself is causing interference.

iReminders

  • Do not disconnect the Field Generator during tracking.
  • Do not coil the Field Generator cable.
  • Leave sufficient slack when connecting cables — don’t strain or place attached cables under tension.
  • Remove EM instruments from the Base Station by holding the connector — don’t pull on the cable.
  • Do not operate within 20 cm of an installed pacemaker.
